question.prompt: Each face of a cube is painted either red or blue, each with probability \(\tfrac12.\) The color of each face is determined independently. What is the probability that the painted cube can be placed on a horizontal surface so that the four vertical faces are all the same color?

solutions.explanation:
Placing the cube on a face makes that face and its opposite the bottom and top. The remaining four faces are vertical. Thus any faces whose color differs from the desired vertical color must fit into one opposite pair.

Count colorings of six fixed faces before moving the cube. There are \(2^6=64\) colorings, each with probability \((\tfrac12)^6\) by independence. Classify them by their color counts.

If all six faces have one color, the cube works. There are \(2\) such colorings.

If exactly one face has the less frequent color, put that face on the bottom. The four vertical faces then have the other color. Choosing the less frequent color and its face gives \(2\cdot6=12\) colorings.

If exactly two faces have the less frequent color, they must be the top and bottom, so they must be opposite. Conversely, any opposite pair can be placed that way. A cube has three opposite pairs, giving \(2\cdot3=6\) colorings.

If there are three faces of each color, neither color supplies four vertical faces, so no placement works.

These cases cover every coloring and are disjoint. We count each coloring once, even if several placements work. Therefore the probability is
\[
\frac{2+12+6}{64}=\frac{20}{64}=\frac{5}{16}.
\]
The answer is \(\frac5{16}\), choice B.
solutions.title: Classify the less frequent color
